headline: UK Health and Care Worker Visa 2026: Requirements, Fees and Rules
metaDescription: UK Health and Care Worker visa 2026: £25,000 salary threshold, B2 English rule, care worker restrictions, application fees, IHS exemption and settlement rules.

sections.content:
The Health and Care Worker visa is the UK's dedicated route for overseas health professionals, offering lower salary thresholds and far lower costs than the standard Skilled Worker visa. To qualify you need a confirmed job offer from a Home Office-licensed sponsor in an eligible occupation code, backed by a Certificate of Sponsorship, and your employer must be the NHS, an NHS supplier or an organisation delivering regulated adult social care.

Eligible roles include doctors, nurses and midwives, pharmacists, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, paramedics, radiographers and other regulated health professionals at graduate skill level. Crucially, care workers and senior care workers are no longer eligible for new overseas sponsorship after the July 2025 rule change — the route is now reserved for registered health professions, not entry-level care roles.
sections.title: Who the Health and Care Worker Visa Is For

sections.content:
There is no single flat rate: your salary must meet whichever is higher of the minimum threshold and the going rate for your occupation code. The threshold stands at £25,000 a year for roles on NHS national pay scales, such as Agenda for Change posts, and £31,300 a year for other health roles, including laboratory technicians. A Band 5 NHS nurse typically earns around £30,000 or more, comfortably above the minimum.

New entrants — workers under 26, recent graduates, trainees and those switching from a UK Student visa — can qualify at discounted rates, provided the salary still clears the relevant absolute minimum. Only guaranteed basic gross pay counts toward the threshold; overtime, on-call payments, bonuses and other allowances are excluded, so structure the offer accordingly.
sections.title: Salary Thresholds for 2026

sections.content:
Since 8 January 2026, new applicants must demonstrate English at CEFR level B2 — reading, writing, speaking and listening — through an approved Secure English Language Test, a degree taught in English, or by nationality. Doctors, dentists, nurses and midwives who have passed the English assessment of their UK professional regulator are exempt from proving it again.

You will also need maintenance funds of £1,270 held for 28 consecutive days, unless your sponsor certifies maintenance or you have lived in the UK for 12 months, plus a criminal record certificate when applying from outside the UK. Applicants from countries such as Pakistan also need a TB test from an approved clinic. The points-based route needs the full 70 points across job offer, salary, occupation and English.
sections.title: English Language and Other Requirements

sections.content:
The fee advantages are substantial: application fees sit around £304 for visas of up to three years and £590 for longer stays, well below standard Skilled Worker rates. Neither you nor your dependants pay the Immigration Health Surcharge at all, a saving worth well over £5,000 across a five-year visa, and your employer pays no Immigration Skills Charge either. Most applications are decided in about three weeks.

The route leads to Indefinite Leave to Remain after five years of continuous residence, provided you remain in eligible employment meeting the salary conditions — currently the same five-year settlement path as the standard Skilled Worker visa. Partners and children can generally join you as dependants, with full IHS exemption for them too, though new partners must meet a basic English requirement.
